  - main:
    - text: EXPRESSION WORKBENCH
    - paragraph: Build an equivalent expression by rationalising the denominator.
    - button "Reset":
      - img
      - text: Reset
    - button "Hint":
      - img
      - text: Hint
    - button "Check":
      - img
      - text: Check
    - complementary:
      - heading "CURRENT EXPRESSION" [level=3]
      - text: 1 √3 + 1 =
      - button "√3 − 1"
      - button "√3 − 1"
      - heading "AVAILABLE TILES (drag to boxes)" [level=3]
      - button "1"
      - button "√3"
      - button "−1"
      - button "√5"
      - button "2"
      - button "√3 − 1"
      - button "√5 − 2"
      - button "2√3"
      - button "2√5"
      - heading "CONJUGATE SELECTOR" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Choose the conjugate of the denominator.
      - radio "√3 + 1 (current denominator)"
      - text: √3 + 1 (current denominator)
      - radio "√3 − 1 (conjugate)" [checked]
      - text: √3 − 1 (conjugate)
      - complementary:
        - img
        - text: TIP Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate to remove the radical.
    - heading "YOUR STEPS (Each step is an equivalent transformation)" [level=3]
    - article:
      - text: "1"
      - strong: Multiply by conjugate
      - text: 1 √3 + 1 × √3 − 1 √3 − 1
    - article:
      - text: "2"
      - strong: Simplify numerator
      - text: √3 − 1 √3 + 1
    - article:
      - text: "3"
      - strong: Simplify denominator (difference of squares)
      - text: √3 − 1 (√3)² − 1²
    - article:
      - text: "4"
      - strong: Simplify
      - text: √3 − 1 2
      - img
    - text: "Well done! The denominator is rational. Final answer: √3 − 1 2 Simplified"
    - img
    - article:
      - heading "KEY RULES" [level=2]
      - text: Multiply by the same nonzero factor
      - paragraph: Multiply numerator and denominator by the same nonzero factor.
      - text: a / b = (a · k) / (b · k), k ≠ 0 Difference of squares (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²
    - article:
      - heading "COMMON MISTAKE" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: COMMON MISTAKE
      - text: Multiplying only the denominator changes the value. 1/(√3 + 1) ≠ 1/2
    - article:
      - heading "WHY IT WORKS" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Multiplying by the conjugate removes the radical using the difference of squares.
      - text: 1/(√3 + 1) × (√3 − 1)/(√3 − 1) = (√3 − 1) / ((√3)² − 1²) = (√3 − 1) / (3 − 1) = (√3 − 1)/2
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
      - text: "Rationalise: 1/(√3 + 1)"
      - paragraph: 1. Multiply by the conjugate
      - text: 1/(√3 + 1) × (√3 − 1)/(√3 − 1)
      - paragraph: 2. Simplify numerator and denominator.
      - text: (√3 − 1)/(3 − 1) = (√3 − 1)/2
    - article:
      - heading "MINI CHALLENGE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Rationalise and verify equivalence.
      - text: "Rationalise: 3/(2 + √5) Your answer"
      - textbox "Your answer": 3(√5 − 2)
      - button "Check equivalence"
      - heading "Numerical check" [level=3]
      - text: Original value 0.708204 Your value 0.708204 Values match! Expressions are equivalent.
      - img
    - complementary:
      - img
      - text: REMEMBER
      - paragraph: Always multiply numerator and denominator by the same nonzero factor. This keeps the value unchanged while removing radicals from the denominator.
      - button "See more practice":
        - text: See more practice
        - img
